title: Grateful Dead Live at Camp Randall Field House, University of Wisconsin on 1971-03-14
venue: Camp Randall Field House, University of Wisconsin
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CDR > EAC(range/high/secure) > CD Wave (split) > SHN v3

ai_review.summary: Crisp 1971 soundboard captures a high‑energy set highlighted by a killer Hurts Me Too, smoking Hard to Handle and an absolute monster Good Lovin’.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clear soundboard tape that delivers excellent vocal clarity and a punchy mix, despite a few harsh cymbal moments and slight channel funkiness on “Hard to Handle.” The show itself brims with primal energy – Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals on “Hurts Me Too,” Jerry’s soaring guitar on the jams, Phil’s wall‑peeling bass line, and an unforgettable, monster rendition of “Good Lovin’” make it a standout 1971 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4‑5) and enthusiastic comments about both the music and sound quality indicate a top‑tier show with only minor sonic quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall crisp and clear mix with excellent vocal clarity; occasional harsh cymbal attack on “Hard to Handle” and slight distortion/funkiness in the channels, but still very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑energy flow throughout; strong second‑half jam on “Hard to Handle” after a tape cut, building into a monster “Good Lovin’.”

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar is described as "really on" with perfect tone and driving the jams hard.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass line is highlighted for peeling walls and carrying the jam to mesmerizing heights.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen delivers primal vocals on “Hurts Me Too” and a standout harmonica moment; also noted for his vocal shout in the performance.
